bibl.title: Toward an integrated classification of neuronal cell types: morphoelectric and transcriptomic characterization of individual GABAergic cortical neurons

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Despite that, the data support the presence of at least 20 interneuron met-types that have congruent morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic properties.

span.label: cortical GABAergic interneuron cell types
span.quote: Neurons are frequently classified into distinct groups or cell types on the basis of structural, physiological, or genetic attributes.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: To establish direct correspondence between the electrical, morphological, and transcriptomic features of mouse cortical neurons, we built a standardized pipeline to extract high quality data from all three modalities from single cells (see Figure 1A, Figure S1, and Methods).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the noisy modality is not clustered on its own but MAPPED onto a reference taxonomy built from the clean one, and the stated purpose is to minimise the contribution of contamination from non-neuronal cells and nearby excitatory neurons
span.quote: To leverage the quality and large size of transcriptomic datasets obtained from dissociated neurons, we chose to map transcriptomes obtained via Patch-seq recordings to transcriptomic types (t-types) derived from analysis of cDNA obtained from dissociated cells (Tasic et al., 2018). This mapping procedure was designed to minimize the contribution of contamination from non-neuronal cells (such as glia) and nearby excitatory neurons.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the mapping is bootstrapped rather than computed once - a hundred iterations, each using only seventy per cent of the available genes and of the reference cells - so that a cell's assigned type carries a confidence instead of being a bare label
span.quote: Next, we mapped Patch-seq transcriptomes to the reference tree via a bootstrap approach in which only 70% of the available genes and reference cells were used in each of 100 iterations.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AMBIGUITY THAT BELONGS TO THE TAXONOMY IS SEPARATED FROM AMBIGUITY THAT BELONGS TO THE MEASUREMENT: a reference matrix records how often each type is confused with each other type in the clean data, and a cell's observed confusion is scored against that expectation rather than against zero
span.quote: To distinguish between “expected” and “unexpected” ambiguity in mapping between t-types, we computed the reference mapping probability matrix between t-types (defined as the probability of a cell type being confused with other cell types in the reference dissociated cell data set). We then used Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the mapping probability distributions and the reference mapping probability distribution as measure of discrepancy.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: two numerical cut-offs then decide which cells are set aside - a divergence above two, and, among the survivors, a correlation below one half between the cell's expression and the average expression of the types
span.quote: Cells assayed via Patch-seq recordings with divergence greater than 2 were considered “inconsistent” cells. For the remaining cells, the correlation between their gene expression and the average gene expression of all the cell types was computed; cells with correlations below 0.5 were also labeled as “inconsistent.”

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the per-type analyses are then run only on the subset with the highest-confidence mapping, and the stated reason is to limit the effect of mapping ambiguities due to technical issues
span.quote: When we performed analyses by t-type, we restricted the data set to the 2,760 cells with highly-consistent mapping to limit the effect mapping ambiguities due to technical issues on our results.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the mapping is checked four separate ways rather than asserted: against a method that does not use the tree's hierarchy at all, against cells from transgenic lines labelling known types, against marker-gene expression levels, and against the layer distribution the dissociated cells show
span.quote: Several results suggested that this mapping approach is meaningful. First, an independent approach that did not rely on the hierarchical structure of the transcriptomic tree assigned cells to similar t-types (Figure S5). Second, cells obtained from transgenic driver mice that label subclasses or specific types of GABAergic interneurons map to similar t-types regardless of whether the examined transcriptomes originated from dissociated cells or Patch-seq recordings (Figure S4). Third, the relative expression level of key marker genes was similar in cells from the two data sets assigned to the same t-type (Figure 1C). Fourth, the layer distribution of cells from Patch-seq recordings that mapped with high confidence to a given ttype closely resembled the layer distribution of dissociated cells mapping to the same t-type

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: whether two named types are electrophysiologically distinct is made TESTABLE rather than assumed: a two-component model, one component per type, is fitted against a single-component model of the two merged, and how much better the split describes the data is then measured as a log-likelihood ratio between the two models
span.quote: Most t-types appeared to have consistent electrophysiological features, but in principle the features of a given t-type could be essentially the same as another. To test whether this was the case, we fit statistical models of pairs of t-types with either two components (one for each t-type) or a single component after merging the t-types together (Methods). We then assessed how much better the two-component model described the data than the single-component model by calculating the log-likelihood ratio (LLR) between the models

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: correspondence between the two classifications is found by spectral co-clustering of the two type sets, with agreement given a stated threshold - at least two thirds of a type's cells falling inside its co-cluster
span.quote: To identify sets of t-types and me-types that corresponded closely to each other, we performed spectral co-clustering (Dhillon, 2001) of t-types and me-types (Figure 6B, gray boxes). Many t-types exhibited good agreement with the co-clusters, defined as having at least two-thirds of their cells within the co-cluster

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE FINAL TYPES ARE EDITED CO-CLUSTERS, NOT CO-CLUSTERS: the poorly-agreeing types are removed first, and the remaining co-clusters are split further wherever the transcriptomic differences inside one are large - so the twenty met-types are the output of a procedure with two further editing steps applied AFTER the clustering, not of the clustering itself
span.quote: The co-clusters of Figure 6B were used as a starting point after removing the t-types with poorer agreement (labeled with gray text). Co-clusters were split further if there were large transcriptomic differences among the types. This procedure resulted in twenty identified met-types

span.label: Too few morphological reconstructions exist for the Vip, Lamp5 and Sncg subclasses, so the number of met-types may change.
span.quote: One is that we do not yet have a sufficiently large number of morphology reconstructions for the Vip, Lamp5 and Sncg subclasses.

span.label: Brain-slice preparation artifacts cannot be ruled out as a source of the observed morphological differences.
span.quote: Moreover, we cannot rule out the possibility that artifacts of the brain slice preparation contribute to or explain observed morphological differences, although the fact that neurons mapping to different met-types (within subclass) exhibit a similar range of total axon lengths suggests that this might not be a major concern.

span.label: Restricting analysis to highly consistent mappings may impose discrete types on what is really continuous variation.
span.quote: However, it is worth noting that some of the ambiguity in types could be biological rather than technical, such that focusing our analysis this way may overly-discretize a landscape with more continuous variation between cells and cell types.

span.label: The field is stated to have no consensus number, or even definition, of neuronal cell types.
span.quote: Despite the diversity and amount of data collected and analyzed to this point, the field has not readily converged on a consensus number, or even definition, of neuronal cell types (Klausberger and Somogyi, 2008); indeed, efforts to determine a consensus number of cell types have been limited by well-documented challenges

span.label: Two modalities counting the same area's interneuron types differ by more than a factor of two.
span.quote: Third, the number of GABAergic cell types estimated from our scRNASeq data (Tasic et al., 2018) and morpho-electric data (Gouwens et al., 2019) collected in mouse primary visual cortex (VISp)- i.e., the number of VISp GABAergic “t-types” (60) and “me-types” (26) - differs by more than a factor of two. Such discrepancies are not unique to VISp; studies applying anatomical, physiological, and neurochemical approaches in other cortical areas have also arrived at varying numbers of GABAergic neuronal types

span.label: A classical cell-type name has no absolute definition, and by the loose reading every met-type would qualify.
span.quote: Note that all these Sst met-types contain at least one cell that has some degree of L1 projection, and therefore could be considered a Martinotti cell as well; we are not aware of an absolute definition of a Martinotti cell in terms of total amount of axon in L1, though it is generally described as “significant”

span.label: The combined classifier's stated improvement is over the morphology arm, not the electrophysiology arm.
span.quote: However, the t-type classifier had a prediction accuracy of 57% (Figure 5B), and prediction error rates varied considerably across t-types. A t-type classifier trained with morphological features only had an accuracy of 41% (Figure 5C), and the pattern of confused types differed from the electrophysiology classifier. The overall lower accuracy could again be in part due to the smaller available number of cells with morphologies. However, classifier accuracy improved to 57% when electrophysiological features were used together with morphological features

span.label: Type frequencies differ between the two preparations despite the same transgenic driver lines.
span.quote: this difference persisted despite using the same, relatively specific transgenic driver lines to label cells under both experimental conditions. Moreover, in several cases, scRNASeq data from PatchSeq recordings mapped more frequently to one t-type (Sst Hpse Cbln4, Pvalb Reln Itm2a) while scRNASeq data from dissociated cells mapped more frequently to another, closely-related t-type (Sst Hpse Sema3c, Pvalb Reln Tac1, respectively). Such discrepancies may reflect gene expression differences in slice versus dissociated cell preparations

span.label: t-types
span.quote: Third, the number of GABAergic cell types estimated from our scRNASeq data (Tasic et al., 2018) and morpho-electric data (Gouwens et al., 2019) collected in mouse primary visual cortex (VISp)- i.e., the number of VISp GABAergic “t-types” (60) and “me-types” (26) - differs by more than a factor of two. Such discrepancies are not unique to VISp; studies applying anatomical, physiological, and neurochemical approaches in other cortical areas have also arrived at varying numbers of GABAergic neuronal types

span.label: me-types
span.quote: Third, the number of GABAergic cell types estimated from our scRNASeq data (Tasic et al., 2018) and morpho-electric data (Gouwens et al., 2019) collected in mouse primary visual cortex (VISp)- i.e., the number of VISp GABAergic “t-types” (60) and “me-types” (26) - differs by more than a factor of two. Such discrepancies are not unique to VISp; studies applying anatomical, physiological, and neurochemical approaches in other cortical areas have also arrived at varying numbers of GABAergic neuronal types

span.label: Martinotti cell
span.quote: Note that all these Sst met-types contain at least one cell that has some degree of L1 projection, and therefore could be considered a Martinotti cell as well; we are not aware of an absolute definition of a Martinotti cell in terms of total amount of axon in L1, though it is generally described as “significant”

span.label: met-types
span.quote: The co-clusters of Figure 6B were used as a starting point after removing the t-types with poorer agreement (labeled with gray text). Co-clusters were split further if there were large transcriptomic differences among the types. This procedure resulted in twenty identified met-types

span.label: co-clusters
span.quote: The co-clusters of Figure 6B were used as a starting point after removing the t-types with poorer agreement (labeled with gray text). Co-clusters were split further if there were large transcriptomic differences among the types. This procedure resulted in twenty identified met-types

span.label: consensus number
span.quote: Despite the diversity and amount of data collected and analyzed to this point, the field has not readily converged on a consensus number, or even definition, of neuronal cell types (Klausberger and Somogyi, 2008); indeed, efforts to determine a consensus number of cell types have been limited by well-documented challenges

span.label: t-type classifier
span.quote: However, the t-type classifier had a prediction accuracy of 57% (Figure 5B), and prediction error rates varied considerably across t-types. A t-type classifier trained with morphological features only had an accuracy of 41% (Figure 5C), and the pattern of confused types differed from the electrophysiology classifier. The overall lower accuracy could again be in part due to the smaller available number of cells with morphologies. However, classifier accuracy improved to 57% when electrophysiological features were used together with morphological features

span.label: a Martinotti cell - A NAMED TYPE WHOSE DEFINING QUANTITY HAS NO THRESHOLD: the quantity is total amount of axon in L1, the criterion on it is the word significant, the authors state they are not aware of an absolute definition, and all the Sst met-types contain at least one cell that could therefore be considered one
span.quote: Note that all these Sst met-types contain at least one cell that has some degree of L1 projection, and therefore could be considered a Martinotti cell as well; we are not aware of an absolute definition of a Martinotti cell in terms of total amount of axon in L1, though it is generally described as “significant”

span.label: a met-type - A CO-CLUSTER THAT WAS THEN EDITED: spectral co-clusters of t-types and me-types were the starting point, t-types with poorer agreement were removed, and co-clusters were split further where transcriptomic differences were large, so the twenty is the output of a procedure with two judgement steps rather than a count of found groups
span.quote: The co-clusters of Figure 6B were used as a starting point after removing the t-types with poorer agreement (labeled with gray text). Co-clusters were split further if there were large transcriptomic differences among the types. This procedure resulted in twenty identified met-types

span.label: the counted number of GABAergic cell types - MODALITY-RELATIVE: for one cortical area of one species it is 60 by transcriptomics and 26 by morpho-electric features, a difference of more than a factor of two, and the authors state other areas have likewise arrived at varying numbers
span.quote: Third, the number of GABAergic cell types estimated from our scRNASeq data (Tasic et al., 2018) and morpho-electric data (Gouwens et al., 2019) collected in mouse primary visual cortex (VISp)- i.e., the number of VISp GABAergic “t-types” (60) and “me-types” (26) - differs by more than a factor of two. Such discrepancies are not unique to VISp; studies applying anatomical, physiological, and neurochemical approaches in other cortical areas have also arrived at varying numbers of GABAergic neuronal types

span.label: extends → Tasic et al. (2018/2016) transcriptomic taxonomy and Gouwens et al. (2019) morpho-electric types
span.quote: Two of our previous efforts have systematically defined neuronal cell types in mouse visual cortex based on either transcriptomic characteristics using a high-throughput scRNAseq pipeline (Tasic et al., 2018; Tasic et al., 2016) or, from a separate standardized pipeline, electrophysiological and morphological characteristics (Gouwens et al., 2019).

span.label: builds-on → Tasic et al. (2018) dissociated-cell transcriptomic reference dataset
span.quote: To leverage the quality and large size of transcriptomic datasets obtained from dissociated neurons, we chose to map transcriptomes obtained via Patch-seq recordings to transcriptomic types (t-types) derived from analysis of cDNA obtained from dissociated cells (Tasic et al., 2018).

span.label: t-types —contrasted-with→ me-types
span.quote: Third, the number of GABAergic cell types estimated from our scRNASeq data (Tasic et al., 2018) and morpho-electric data (Gouwens et al., 2019) collected in mouse primary visual cortex (VISp)- i.e., the number of VISp GABAergic “t-types” (60) and “me-types” (26) - differs by more than a factor of two. Such discrepancies are not unique to VISp; studies applying anatomical, physiological, and neurochemical approaches in other cortical areas have also arrived at varying numbers of GABAergic neuronal types

span.label: met-types —operationalised-as→ co-clusters
span.quote: The co-clusters of Figure 6B were used as a starting point after removing the t-types with poorer agreement (labeled with gray text). Co-clusters were split further if there were large transcriptomic differences among the types. This procedure resulted in twenty identified met-types

span.label: sparse principal component analysis
span.quote: Sparse principal component analysis was performed separately on each data set.

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: The dimensionality of the data sets was reduced by performing principal components analysis (PCA) on the set of elecrophysiological or morphological features and keeping the top three principal components.

span.label: likelihood ratio test
span.quote: We then assessed how much better the two-component model described the data than the single-component model by calculating the log-likelihood ratio (LLR) between the models (Figure 3E).

span.label: bootstrap
span.quote: Since the two-component model would produce a higher likelihood due to overfitting even if the underlying distributions were the same, the statistical significance of the observed LLR was assessed by parametric boostrap.

span.label: p-value
span.quote: The statistical significance of the improvement was assessed by parametric bootstrap; pairs that do not exceed statistical significance levels of p=0.05 and p=0.001 are indicated by crosses and slashes, respectively.

span.label: random forest classifier
span.quote: Supervised classification was performed by training a random-forest classifier with 100 trees using balanced class weights, implemented with the scikit-learn Python package (Pedregosa et al., 2011).

span.label: cross-validation
span.quote: To assess the degree to which pairs of t-types exhibited discrete or continuous variation in electrophysiological and morphological feature space, we used a cross-validated discriminant analysis method based on one developed to address a similar question in transcriptomic feature space (Harris et al., 2018).

span.label: discriminability index (effect size)
span.quote: then summarized the separation of those likelihood ratios by a d(cid:48) statistic (Figure 5E; higher values indicate more separation).

span.label: correlation
span.quote: To test how consistent morphologies were within a t-type, we measured the correlation between an individual cell’s axon histogram and the t-type average (Figure 4B).

span.label: Kullback-Leibler divergence
span.quote: We then used Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the mapping probability distributions and the reference mapping probability distribution as measure of discrepancy.

span.label: Jensen-Shannon divergence
span.quote: For the t-types with good me-type consistency, we asked whether t-types in the same co-cluster were also transcriptomically similar, as determined by their Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence (Figure 6C; see also Figure S12).

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: Histograms are shown as mean (lines) ± SEM (shaded regions).

span.label: resampling / subsampling for cluster stability
span.quote: Clusters were evaluated for stability by repeating the entire procedure on 90% subsamples and calculated the average Jaccard similarity; clusters with average Jaccard similarities below 0.5 were considered unstable and merged with another closest-matching cluster.

span.label: The combined data support at least twenty GABAergic interneuron met-types whose transcriptomic, electrophysiological and morphological properties agree.
span.quote: Altogether, our results support the presence of at least 20 GABAergic interneuron met-types that have congruent transcriptomic, electrophysiological and morphological properties (Figure 7).

span.label: Nine met-types were resolved within the Sst subclass alone, roughly double the number of Sst types described by earlier morphological or electrophysiological work.
span.quote: Analysis of this dataset supports the presence of nine Sst met-types (Figure 7)

span.label: Sst neurons respect laminar boundaries, and which layer their axon dominantly targets discriminates among them better than whether or not they send axon to layer 1.
span.quote: These results reveal that Sst neurons highly respect laminar boundaries across cortex, they have clear laminar innervation preferences that differ based on their met-type and/or laminar position, and that their dominant laminar target may be a more reliable feature for distinguishing among Sst neurons than the presence or absence of axon in layer 1.

span.label: Most transcriptomic types are electrophysiologically distinguishable from one another, with non-significant pairs largely confined to sibling types on the same branch of the taxonomy.
span.quote: Most pairs were significantly better fit by separate distributions for each t-type rather than by a single distribution describing the pair, indicating that most t-types systematically differed from each other in their electrophysiological properties.

span.label: Electrophysiology predicts transcriptomic subclass very well but individual t-type poorly, and adding morphology does not improve t-type prediction.
span.quote: However, classifier accuracy improved to 57% when electrophysiological features were used together with morphological features (Figure 5D).

span.label: Cells of the same t-type have similar morpho-electric properties, yet a cell's specific t-type usually cannot be read off those properties.
span.quote: At the same time, it is frequently difficult to predict the specific t-type of a neuron based on morphological and/or physiological features (Figures 5 and 6).

span.label: Somata of many GABAergic t-types occupy specific laminar or sublaminar positions, giving an anatomical correlate to purely transcriptomic groupings.
span.quote: The specific laminar (or sublaminar) locations of many GABAergic t-types across subclasses provides a strong anatomical correlate of the cell groupings defined based on transcriptomic data alone.

span.label: Individual cells' axon depth histograms correlate positively with their t-type average, indicating consistent innervation patterns within a type.
span.quote: Most cells were positively correlated, indicating consistent axonal innervation patterns.

span.label: met-type (morphological/electrophysiological/transcriptomic type)
span.quote: We used these results to define morphological/electrophysiological/transcriptomic types (mettypes) that exhibited a high degree of congruence across all three examined modalities.

span.label: t-type (transcriptomic type)
span.quote: we chose to map transcriptomes obtained via Patch-seq recordings to transcriptomic types (t-types) derived from analysis of cDNA obtained from dissociated cells (Tasic et al., 2018).

span.label: "inconsistent" cell (mapping-quality category)
span.quote: Cells assayed via Patch-seq recordings with divergence greater than 2 were considered “inconsistent” cells.

span.label: Patch-seq recording technique
span.quote: Moreover, new methods such as the Patch-seq recording technique (Fuzik et al., 2016; Cadwell et al., 2016; Scala et al., 2019; F ¨oldy et al., 2016) enable one to directly relate the transcriptomic features of a given neuron to other identifying characteristics of the same neuron

span.label: transcriptomic type (t-type) assignment of each cell
span.term: transcriptomic type (t-type) assignment of each cell
span.quote: we chose to map transcriptomes obtained via Patch-seq recordings to transcriptomic types (t-types) derived from analysis of cDNA obtained from dissociated cells (Tasic et al., 2018).

span.label: intrinsic electrophysiological features (responses to square-pulse current injections)
span.term: intrinsic electrophysiological features (responses to square-pulse current injections)
span.quote: we analyzed all 3,708 neurons’ electrophysiological responses to a standardized currentclamp protocol composed of square-pulse current injections (see Figure S6 for example responses by t-type).

span.label: morphological features (dendrite and axon laminar distribution)
span.term: morphological features (dendrite and axon laminar distribution)
span.quote: For a subset (350 cells) of transcriptomically and electrophysiologically characterized neurons from the Sst, Pvalb, Vip, Sncg, and Lamp5 subclasses, we also performed morphological analysis.

span.label: soma location and cortical depth in the Allen Mouse Common Coordinate Framework
span.term: soma location and cortical depth in the Allen Mouse Common Coordinate Framework
span.quote: Specifically, many t-types were distinguished by a layer-selective axonal projection.

span.label: mapping-quality / QC criteria used to admit cells to analysis
span.term: mapping-quality / QC criteria used to admit cells to analysis
span.quote: Cells assayed via Patch-seq recordings with divergence greater than 2 were considered “inconsistent” cells.

span.label: 3,708 — cortical GABAergic interneurons whose transcriptomic and electrophysiological data passed quality control; 350 of them were morphologically reconstructed
span.quote: Both the transcriptomic and electrophysiological data from 3,708 cortical GABAergic interneurons passed our QC criteria (see Methods and Figure S1A ); the 2341 cells that exhibited adequate biocytin filling were imaged at 63X resolution, and the dendritic and axonal morphologies of 350 of these cells were reconstructed.

span.label: 3,417 of the 3,708 — cells mapped to one or more reference transcriptomic types with better than 70% confidence
span.quote: We found that 3,417 of the 3,708 cells (2,760 “highly consistent” and 657 “moderately consistent” cells in Figure S1G) were mapped to one or more than one type with more than 70% confidence (Figure S3, Methods).

span.label: >90% — accuracy of the random forest classifier predicting transcriptomic subclass from electrophysiological features
span.quote: The subclass classifier performed at >90% accuracy (Figure 5A), indicating that GABAergic transcriptomic subclasses have distinctive electrophysiological features.

span.label: 57% — accuracy of the classifier predicting individual t-type from electrophysiological features
span.quote: However, the t-type classifier had a prediction accuracy of 57% (Figure 5B), and prediction error rates varied considerably across t-types.

span.label: 41% — accuracy of the classifier predicting t-type from morphological features alone
span.quote: A t-type classifier trained with morphological features only had an accuracy of 41% (Figure 5C), and the pattern of confused types differed from the electrophysiology classifier.

span.label: 57% — accuracy of the classifier when electrophysiological and morphological features were combined - no better than electrophysiology alone
span.quote: However, classifier accuracy improved to 57% when electrophysiological features were used together with morphological features (Figure 5D).

span.label: 83% — share of the authors' Patch-seq recordings made in primary visual cortex, the remainder in surrounding higher visual areas
span.quote: For example, 83% of our Patch-seq recordings were

span.label: (60) and (26) — previously estimated numbers of VISp GABAergic transcriptomic types versus morpho-electric types, the discrepancy this study set out to resolve
span.quote: the number of VISp GABAergic “t-types” (60) and “me-types” (26) - differs by more than a factor of two

span.label: twenty — met-types produced by the co-clustering plus transcriptomic-splitting procedure
span.quote: This procedure resulted in twenty identified met-types (Figure 7).
